statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ is quoted at 29,204.25 and 29,205.50, up 98.50 to 99.75 points or 0.34% on the 29,105.75 settle, after printing a third consecutive higher overnight high at 29,225.00 and holding within about 20 points of it. Repeated extension while trading near a session extreme is the amplifier this measure watches, and it has now persisted across three hours. The counter-evidence keeps the reading in the low band: the entire overnight range is 29,017.00 to 29,225.00, roughly 208 points or 0.71%, and Asia has repaired rather than trended, with the Nikkei 225 at 65,808.59 up 0.43% from a 64,609.47 low and the KOSPI at 6,655.64 down only 0.62% from a 6,408.82 low. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0%, the 10-year is near 4.71% and the 2-year near 4.26%, and WTI is $84.96 with Brent $92.03 after the announced Iran sanctions campaign imposed no immediate penalties. Tail sits at 14 with Stress at 45, which holds the mapped state below the block threshold.
recommendation: Descriptive only. The observation that carries this hour is that the overnight extension has continued rather than failed. Three hours ago NQ printed 29,168.25, two hours ago 29,197.00, and the contract has now traded 29,225.00 while sitting within roughly 20 points of that high. Extension, brief pause, then a fresh high is the shape this measure treats as Tail-relevant, and it is the reason Tail is carried up one point to 14 rather than allowed to decay. Three things hold the reading well inside the low band. The amplitude is small: 208 points across the whole overnight session is about 0.71%, so the directional efficiency is operating on a narrow range and every leg has been a slow grind rather than an impulse. The regional backdrop is repairing, not aligning: the Nikkei has recovered about 1.9% off its low to trade positive, and the KOSPI about 3.9% off its own low, having been down 2.7% earlier in the session. That is two-sided behaviour, the opposite of the no-retracement path this measure is built to detect. And the cross-asset set is de-escalating rather than confirming: VIX fell 6.0% to 14.89, yields are off their recent highs with the 10-year at 4.71%, and oil slipped after the Iran sanctions announcement produced rhetoric without immediate penalties. Today's US calendar carries no high-impact release, so the narrow window around the cash open and the 14:00Z medium-impact cluster is where conditional risk concentrates. Wednesday's Core PCE, second GDP estimate and durable goods print, followed by Nvidia after the close, sit beyond this horizon and are carried as Stress rather than Tail.
headline: NQ extends to a third consecutive overnight high at 29,225 and holds within 20 points of it, but Asia repairs off its lows and VIX drops 6.0% to 14.89; Tail 14 and Stress 45 into a US session with no high-impact release
body:
The decisive observation this hour is that the overnight extension sequence is intact. Yahoo Finance shows NQ at 29,205.50, up 99.75 points or 0.34%, and Investing.com shows 29,204.25, up 98.50 points or 0.34%, on the 29,105.75 settle. The overnight band has widened to 29,017.00-29,225.00, and the 29,225.00 high is the third successive higher extreme after 29,168.25 and 29,197.00 in the two preceding hours. Price is sitting in the top tenth of that band. Repeated extension combined with holding near the extreme is exactly the structure this measure treats as evidence that retracements are becoming shallow, so Tail is carried up from 13 to 14.

What prevents that from becoming a larger move is amplitude and context. A 208-point overnight range is about 0.71%, which is unremarkable, and each leg higher has taken roughly an hour rather than arriving as an impulse. More importantly, the regional session has been strongly two-sided. Reuters reported early in the Asian day that the Nikkei was down 0.9% and the KOSPI down 2.7% on chip nerves, Alibaba's discounted $10.2 billion share sale and Samsung's shareholder-return disappointment. Since then the Nikkei has recovered to 65,808.59, up 0.43% and about 1.9% above its 64,609.47 low, and the KOSPI has recovered to 6,655.64, down only 0.62% and about 3.9% above its 6,408.82 low. Markets that fall and then repair most of the loss inside one session are the definition of functioning mean reversion.

The cross-asset set is de-escalating rather than aligning behind equities. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0% from 15.84, having traded as low as 14.77. Treasury yields are off their recent highs after reporting that the Treasury may fund expanded buybacks from its General Account, with the 10-year near 4.71% and the 2-year near 4.26%. WTI is $84.96 and Brent $92.03, both slightly lower, after the announced campaign to cut Iran out of the global economy arrived with sanctions designations but no immediate penalties on third countries and with mediation talks reported in Tehran. Shared Finviz cross-asset context, collected at 05:19Z and treated as delayed supporting evidence only, is consistent with this: index futures modestly higher, VIX futures slightly lower, Treasury futures marginally softer, and a latest-session semiconductor complex that was uniformly negative with all seven tracked names lower and a mean change of -3.0%.

The conditional path holds inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours. It eases into the Japanese close, lifts to 15 at the European cash open because that hour produced the largest reading of the preceding 24, and then steps down to a floor of 12 through the European midday. It rebuilds from 12:00Z as Fed Barkin and the weekly ADP print arrive, reaches 17 at 13:00Z for Case-Shiller and the cash open, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z where CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and the Richmond Fed index all land thirty minutes into cash trade. That peak remains below the block threshold because every US release today is medium impact and, on this measure's calibration, event importance and forecast dispersion raise Stress and reduce Confidence before they raise Tail. The overnight hours then fall back to 11 before drifting up to 14 by the close of the horizon as Wednesday's Core PCE, second GDP estimate and durable goods cluster, and Nvidia's results after the US close, come into view. Options are pricing a 5.4% post-earnings move in Nvidia against a 7.4% twelve-quarter average, which is a comparatively contained expectation for the single largest index constituent.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 05:00Z on 24 August with Tail 9 and Stress 39 in a normal mode. Its first structural peak came at 07:00Z, where the European cash open produced Tail 19 with Stress 58 in a trend-down mode; that faded to 17 within an hour and to 12 by 09:00Z, holding an 11 to 13 band through the European morning. The window's only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z, which mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z, which reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode and mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That peak decayed immediately, to 13 by 15:00Z and into single digits from 17:00Z onward as the US afternoon mean-reverted, running a 7 to 9 Tail band with Stress easing from 46 to 42. The overnight hours since have held a 9 to 13 band with Stress steady near 45 to 47, closing the window at 04:00Z with Tail 13 in a trend-up mode as the overnight extension sequence began.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 14 on the observed third consecutive overnight high, eases to 13 into the Japanese cash close, and lifts to 15 at 07:00Z for the European cash open, the same hour that produced the largest reading of the preceding 24. It then steps down through the European morning to a floor of 12 at 10:00Z and 11:00Z, the calendar-empty part of the day. The series rebuilds to 14 at 12:00Z for the Barkin and weekly ADP checkpoints, reaches 17 at 13:00Z as Case-Shiller prints and the US cash open follows at 13:30Z, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z for the CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. That is the highest conditional reading of the horizon and it still sits below the block threshold, because today's US calendar carries no high-impact release and no post-event price path can be observed in advance. It decays to 16 and then 14 through the US morning, holds 13 to 14 across the afternoon, the 17:00Z two-year auction and the power hour, and falls to 11 after the cash close. The overnight stretch runs 11 to 12 before drifting to 13 and then 14 in the final two slots as Wednesday's Core PCE, second GDP estimate and durable goods cluster, and Nvidia's results after that day's close, come into view. Stress traces the same shape one band higher, from 44 overnight to a 56 peak at 14:00Z and back to 51 at the horizon's end, while Confidence decays from 87 to 68 with distance from observed evidence. The narrow danger window is 13:30Z to 14:30Z, spanning the cash open and the medium-impact release cluster.
